description: Four polarizers, each scaling its input by a bipolar level so the channel attenuates, inverts or ring modulates, with the outputs normalled downward so they mix

params.text: Picks the voltage an unpatched channel input is normalled to, 5V or 10V
Picks how the level CV is read: unipolar clamped from 0V to unity, which gives a plain two quadrant VCA, bipolar clamped, or bipolar with no limit
Picks the CV voltage that counts as 100%, 5V or 10V
Cycles output clipping through off, hard at 10V, hard at 5V, soft tanh saturation at 12V and soft tanh saturation at 6V
Sets that channel's level between -100% and 100%, negative values inverting the input; the CV adds to it and the total is clamped at 200% either way
Attenuates and inverts that channel's level CV before it is added to the level knob
Cycles oversampling of every input and output through off, x2, x4, x8, x16 and x32, to control the aliasing that ring modulation or clipping would otherwise produce

inputs.text: CV added to the level knob through its attenuator, with unity being the voltage picked by the U button
The channel input that the level scales; left unpatched it becomes the constant voltage picked by the N button, so the channel gives an offset instead

outputs.text: That channel's input scaled by its net level; leave this jack unpatched and the signal is passed down and mixed into the next patched output below

menu: Oversample filter quality — 10th order by default, with 8th order and a cheaper 6th order; 10th and 8th cut at 80% of Nyquist and 6th at 50%; it works only while oversampling is on
